summary: Today’s pulse tracks House lawmakers return to Capitol Hill as Republicans hope to pass stopgap spending bill – live, Two dead and more than a dozen missing after 'terrifying' flash flood hits Grand Canyon, and Conservative reshuffle: who’s who in Kemi Badenoch’s top team. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are santos, missing, and badenoch. In the background, Turkish deep-sea search vessel joins efforts to retrieve 20 still missing after Cyprus ferry disaster and Kalshi bans ex-congressman George Santos from prediction platform for life keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: House lawmakers return to Capitol Hill as Republicans hope to pass stopgap spending bill – live
headlines.description: The US House is back after a five-week recess; government funding is guaranteed through 30 September

headlines.title: Two dead and more than a dozen missing after 'terrifying' flash flood hits Grand Canyon
headlines.description: "It was a beautiful day - and then people were screaming," one hiker tells the BBC, as 14 people are missing.

headlines.title: Conservative reshuffle: who’s who in Kemi Badenoch’s top team?
headlines.description: From a darling of the Tory right to a moderate former army officer, we profile the key players Andrew Griffith and Tom Tugendhat join Badenoch’s top team in Tory reshuffle Kemi Badenoch has kicked off the return to parliament with a reshuffle of her top team in order to take on Andy Burnham and Reform UK. She has made sweeping changes to the shadow cabinet and ruthlessly axed her shadow chancellor. Here is a run-down of the new characters sitting across from Labour on the opposition frontbench.

headlines.title: Turkish deep-sea search vessel joins efforts to retrieve 20 still missing after Cyprus ferry disaster
headlines.description: TCG Isin expected to play vital role in locating Filo Jet’s voyage data recorder 514 metres below surface A deep-sea search and rescue vessel is on its way to Cyprus as Turkey joins efforts to retrieve the 20 people still missing after a passenger ferry capsized off the island’s northern coast. The TCG Isin will join the vast operation to find survivors after the high-speed ferry sank on Sunday barely four nautical miles outside the port town of Kyrenia.

headlines.title: Kalshi bans ex-congressman George Santos from prediction platform for life
headlines.description: Santos was accused of profiting from bets tied to his attendance at Trump’s State of the Union address George Santos, the former Republican congressman whose political career collapsed under a mountain of lies, has become the first person ever handed a lifetime ban by the prediction-market platform Kalshi. The company announced the permanent suspension on Monday, along with a $71,356 fine, after federal regulators accused Santos of profiting from bets tied to his own attendance at Donald Trump’s State of the Union address earlier this year.

headlines.title: Ex-congressman George Santos banned from betting platform for life
headlines.description: The prediction market operator Kalshi says Santos made barred trades and misleading comments that influenced prices.

headlinePool.title: More public control is only way to grow UK economy, Burnham to tell MPs
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: Prime minister wants to ‘bring back hope’ by tackling cost of living as MPs call for electoral reform Andy Burnham will drive home his pledge to bring more essential services back into public control, telling MPs in the Commons on Tuesday that it will be the only way to improve growth across the country. Burnham will address the house for the first time in 16 years from the frontbench, and six weeks since he became prime minister, after spending the summer recess announcing a slew of policies that will now be put before MPs.

headlinePool.title: Andrew Griffith and Tom Tugendhat join Badenoch’s top team in Tory reshuffle
headlinePool.description: Conservative leader sacks shadow chancellor Mel Stride and shadow foreign secretary Priti Patel Kemi Badenoch sacked her shadow chancellor, Mel Stride, and the shadow foreign secretary, Priti Patel, in a sweeping Conservative reshuffle on Monday, replacing Stride with Andrew Griffith, and Patel with Tom Tugendhat. Stride, who had been shadow chancellor since Badenoch became leader, was widely seen among Tories as failing to make an impression at a time when Labour had been under pressure over the economy.

headlinePool.title: Two dead and at least 15 missing after flash flood in Arizona’s Grand Canyon
headlinePool.description: National Park Service confirms second death from weekend flash flood as area braces for more storms A second death was confirmed by National Park Service officials on Monday after aflash flood sent a surge of water and debris through an area of the Grand Canyon over the weekend. Dozens of visitors had to be evacuated by helicopter during the deluge that consumed trails and infrastructure. Fifteen people are still missing or unaccounted for, as more heavy rain and thunderstorms in the forecasts threaten additional debris flows, flash floods or rockfalls , the NPS said in a statement.

headlinePool.title: Congressional nominee Brad Lander heckled over Israel stance at New York protest
headlinePool.description: Lander screamed at and verbally abused as he protested against Hindu nationalist rally in Madison Square Garden The New York Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander was screamed at and verbally abused by protesters over his stance on Israel as he protested against a Hindu nationalist politician speaking outside Madison Square Garden. As Lander attended a demonstration on Saturday against the event, organized by the Hindu nationalist RSS movement and where Mohan Bhagwat, leader of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh was speaking, he was confronted by several protesters demanding that he leave the rally.

headlinePool.title: Police appeal after unidentified woman’s body found in Liverpool park
headlinePool.description: Body of victim thought to be in her 70s found in bin bag in walled garden area of Stanley Park on Friday Police in Liverpool have urged members of the public to come forward with information after the body of an unknown woman believed to be in her 70s was found in a black bin bag in a popular park. Merseyside police were contacted by a passerby who had found the woman’s body in Stanley Park, in the Anfield area of Liverpool, at about 5.25pm on Friday 28 August.

headlinePool.title: US singer D4vd's celebrity lawyers withdraw from murder case
headlinePool.description: The singer, 21, will be now represented by a public defender in the murder trial of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. He has pleaded not guilty.

headlinePool.title: Trump says datacenter opponents ‘want to end up being backwards and poor’
headlinePool.description: Three-quarters of Americans said in a recent poll that they oppose datacenters being built next to their homes Donald Trump has criticized communities pushing back against datacenter projects across the US amid a growing backlash, warning those that reject them risk becoming “backwards and poor”. As controversy surrounding local datacenter plans continues to swirl around election campaigns nationwide ahead of November’s midterm elections, the US president declared Americans “will only have yourselves to blame” if they are canceled.

headlinePool.title: Nepal rescuers blast hillside in search of hydropower workers as families wait anxiously
headlinePool.description: Rescuers have resorted to explosives as they struggle to reach trapped workers, as the flooding death toll reaches 939.

headlinePool.title: Trump says US will ‘hit Iran hard’ as hostilities resume – as it happened
headlinePool.description: Iran responded to an assault on its Larak Island by targeting US bases in Jordan Trump threatens further action as US and Iran exchange fire in new flare-up Coinciding with this week’s G20 meeting , the EU has issued a statement saying it will work with the US and other allied countries to maintain economic pressure against Iran. “The ‌EU welcomes efforts at ensuring that Iran ceases its destabilising activities and engages in peace negotiations with good ‌faith, also through additional economic pressure, including through ​the US-led Operation Economic Outcast,” it said in reference to the pressure strategy the White House describes as “an unprecedented campaign to sever every remaining economic lifeline sustaining” the Islamic republic.
